newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares open sideways, trapped in range.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares open sideways, trapped in range.

text.p: Singapore shares opened very slightly higher on Thursday in thin volume.
Dealers said the market appeared to be trapped within a tight range between 2,090 and 2,120 and was unlikely to break out of it in the absence of fresh market-moving news.
"I think the market could bounce today but not by much," said one dealer. "The volume is very limited and foreign buyers seem to be keeping away for the time being."
By 0150 GMT, the key Straits Times Industrials Index (STII) was 3.49 points higher at 2,106.45 with 11.6 million shares traded. Gainers led losers by 76 to 19.
Dealers said the STII appeared to be consolidating ahead of a possible rise in the medium-term.
"From a sentiment point of view I think buying is not far off, but overseas demand is not evident yet," said a dealer.
Of the 30 STII stocks, drinks firm Fraser & Neave and marine-based group Keppel Corp both rose 10 cents to Singapore $14.00 and S$10.30 respectively.
Near the top of the actives list was United Pulp & Paper, which rose six cents to S$1.79 after reporting a tripling of net profit for the half-year to June 30.
